title: Flat scalar extension and compatible projective Hom models
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Use ordinary module derived categories with localization functors $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], or equivalently the one-object bottom-topology module-sheaf categories [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]. Write $F(C)=S\otimes_R C$ termwise, $U$ for restriction of scalars, and $LF=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ for derived extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every unbounded cochain complex $C$, tensoring the inclusions and quotients defining its cycles $Z^iC=\ker d_C^i$ and boundaries $B^iC=\operatorname{im}d_C^{i-1}$ gives natural identifications $Z^i(FC)=S\otimes_R Z^iC$, $B^i(FC)=S\otimes_R B^iC$, and $H^i(FC)\cong S\otimes_RH^i(C)$. Consequently $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and there is a natural isomorphism $c_C:LF(Q_RC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(FC)$. Its normalization is that for every K-flat resolution $k:K\to C$, $c_C$ is the K-flat model comparison followed by $Q_S(Fk)$; these comparisons are compatible with changing resolutions. The adjunction $LF\dashv U$ has, under $c$, unit represented by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and counit represented by $s\otimes y\mapsto sy$.

Let $P$ be a bounded-above complex of projective $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and $N$ any unbounded $R$-complex. Put $H_R=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,N)$ and $H_S=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN)$, using the product total Hom [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], identified with [def-pur-hom-complex] on the one-object site. Then $FP$ is bounded above with projective terms, and the canonical projective-Hom model comparisons give isomorphisms
$$Q_RH_R\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_RP,Q_RN),\qquad Q_SH_S\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LF(Q_RP),LF(Q_RN)),$$
where derived internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the second comparison uses $c_P,c_N$. These comparisons are natural in the representatives and compatible with localization. The same $R$-linear Hom model applies with target $U(FN)$; no boundedness or K-flatness assumption on $N$ or $H_R$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0A66 (lemma-RHom-out-of-projective), with Tag 0GMT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint); flat exact-extension model refinement from the proof of lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with the flat $R$-module $S$ to the sequences $0\to Z^iC\to C^i\to B^{i+1}C\to0$ and $0\to B^iC\to Z^iC\to H^iC\to0$. Thus $F$ preserves these exact sequences, including their injections and surjections. Factor $F(d_C^i)$ as $FC^i\twoheadrightarrow F B^{i+1}C\hookrightarrow FC^{i+1}$. Its kernel is the image of $F Z^iC\hookrightarrow FC^i$ and its image is the indicated copy of $F B^{i+1}C$. This proves the asserted identifications of cycles and boundaries, as submodules via their specified inclusions.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), applied to the cycle and boundary short exact sequences

proof.text: The second exact sequence of step 1 identifies the quotient $Z^i(FC)/B^i(FC)$ with $F H^i(C)$. A chain map induces maps of both short exact sequences; hence the quotient identification is natural, with the prescribed cycle inclusion and cohomology projection. If $a:C\to C'$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $H^i(Fa)$ is identified with $F(H^i(a))$, which is invertible for every $i$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Fa$ is a quasi-isomorphism. No bound on the index $i$ was used.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat); cohomology as cycles modulo boundaries

proof.text: The tensor functor is additive, and step 1 shows it is exact; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] therefore gives its termwise localization $D(F)$. The cited nodes use $T(C)=C\otimes_RS$; the termwise symmetry $\tau_C:S\otimes_RC\to C\otimes_RS$, $s\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes s$, is a natural isomorphism of complexes $F\cong T$, and below $F(k)$ means $\tau^{-1}T(k)\tau$, $Q_S\tau$ being absorbed into $c$. Apply [lem-trf-ringed-scalar-universal-resolution-comparison] on the singleton site, identified with modules by [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]. Write $\varepsilon_C:LF(Q_RC)\to Q_SFC$ for its universal comparison. For every K-flat resolution $k:K\to C$ the cited statement gives $\varepsilon_C=Q_S(Fk)\theta_k$, where $\theta_k:LF(Q_RC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_SFK$ is the K-flat model comparison. Step 2 makes $Q_S(Fk)$ invertible. Hence $c_C=\varepsilon_C$ is invertible for every $C$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ gives a natural isomorphism $LF\cong D(F)$. The cited formulas for $\theta_k$ give precisely the requested resolution normalization, compatibility with augmentations, and three-resolution cocycle, including K-flat resolutions without flat terms.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual universal comparison; counit formulas of lem-trf-ringed-scalar-universal-resolution-comparison

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] on the singleton site via [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]. It gives the specified $LF\dashv U$, and the unit and adjunct formulas on K-flat representatives with flat terms. Such a resolution $k:K\to C$ exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $u_C(x)=1\otimes x$, the image under $\tau^{-1}$ of the cited $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; likewise $\tau$ turns the cited $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,g(x)$ into $a\otimes x\mapsto a\,g(x)$. Naturality of the unit and of $c$ gives $U(c_C)\eta_{Q_RC}Q_Rk=U(Q_SFk)Q_Ru_K=Q_Ru_C Q_Rk$; cancel the isomorphism $Q_Rk$. Thus under $c_C$ the unit is $Q_Ru_C$ for arbitrary $C$. For an $S$-complex $Y$, resolve $UY$ by $g:K\to UY$ with flat-term K-flat $K$. The cited counit formula is $\epsilon_{Q_SY}=Q_S(m_Y Fg)\theta_g$, where $m_Y(s\otimes y)=sy$. Step 3 gives $c_{UY}=Q_S(Fg)\theta_g$, so $\epsilon_{Q_SY}=Q_S(m_Y)c_{UY}$. These are the claimed representatives. The two degreewise triangle identities send $s\otimes x$ to $s\otimes x$ and $y$ to $y$; both formulas use the same $c$, not a separately chosen adjunction.

source.place: Tag 0GMT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), normalized representative formulas

proof.text: Choose $b$ with $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. Then $(FP)^i=F(0)=0$ for $i>b$. For each $i$, [lem-trf-local-projective-tensor-base-change] applied to $R\to S$ and $P^i$ says that $S\otimes_RP^i$ is projective over $S$. Thus $FP$ satisfies the same bounded-above projective-source hypotheses over $S$. This use requires no finite-generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective), scalar extension of a direct summand of a free module

proof.text: By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_RP,Q_RN)$ is the complex $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,I(N))$ for the fixed K-injective resolution $\eta_N:N\to I(N)$; the canonical model comparison is $Q_R\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,\eta_N):Q_RH_R\to Q_R\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,I(N))$, as in the source proof of 0A66. It is invertible: [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] for $(R,P,N)$ and $(R,P,I(N))$ gives isomorphisms of $Q_RH_R$ and $Q_R\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,I(N))$ to the adjoint internal Hom of $(Q_RP,Q_RN)$ and $(Q_RP,Q_RI(N))$, natural in the target, and the adjoint internal Hom of the isomorphism $Q_R\eta_N$ is invertible; the naturality square makes $Q_R\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,\eta_N)$ invertible. The same argument for $(S,FP,FN)$, valid by step 5, gives $Q_SH_S\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q_SFP,Q_SFN)$. Compose the second isomorphism with $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(c_P,c_N^{-1})$; contravariance in the first variable gives exactly the stated target with $LF(Q_RP),LF(Q_RN)$. The module product Hom agrees with [def-pur-hom-complex] on the singleton site: a sheaf is its sole module, a sheaf Hom section is a module-linear map, the products are sectionwise, and both differentials are $d_Nf-(-1)^{|f|}fd_P$. Thus these are the internal-Hom models of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], not just identifications of groups of morphisms.

The two applications in step 6 are natural in their source and target representatives by [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model]; step 3 makes the two $c$ factors natural as well. For a target quasi-isomorphism, its derived image is invertible, so the naturality square makes the corresponding Hom-model map invertible after localization. For a derived morphism between bounded-above projective source representatives, [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] represents it by a chain map uniquely up to homotopy. If $a-b=d_Ph+hd_{P\prime}$, the operator $T(f)=(-1)^{|f|}fh$ satisfies $dT+Td=f(a-b)$ on total Hom by expansion. Hence precomposition is independent of the representing chain map after localization. Naturality for inverse quasi-isomorphisms follows by inverting the square. Finally apply the same projective-Hom theorem over $R$ with target $U(FN)$. Its target may be any complex, so neither $N$, $U(FN)$, nor $H_R$ needs to be bounded or K-flat.
